findings.detail: The question repeats the problem of earlier questions M2-S49-T2 and M3-S13-T2 in a code review setting. The correct action is the same: per-item confidence from the verification pass, with thresholds calibrated on a labeled validation set. More than one wrong option also repeats. Option C (the same session re-checks itself and routes by agreement between passes) repeats option D of M2-S49-T2. Option D (one aggregate score per review) repeats the per-document verdict in option A of M2-S49-T2. The same reasoning leads to the answer.

blind_answer.reason: One review-level score lumps strong and weak findings together, so the fix is to score and route each finding on its own. Option B gives every finding its own confidence level and routes it against thresholds calibrated on a labeled validation set (4.6-S3, 5.5-S3). A asks for generic conservatism, which does not improve precision (4.1-K2). C relies on self-review in the same session, which is a known limitation (4.6-K1). D raises the threshold but still routes whole reviews rather than individual findings.
